acceptOwnership().details: The new owner accepts the ownership transfer.

addExemptAddress(address).details: Reverts if the address is already exempt, matching the single-item convention used elsewhere in the library. `address(0)` is rejected: it is the mint/burn sentinel, never a holder.

addExemptAddresses(address[]).details: Duplicates are skipped and counted rather than reverting; `address(0)` rejects the whole batch. Both follow the library-wide batch convention.

returns._0: True if `restrictionCode` is one of this rule's codes.

returns.isValid: => true if the transfer is valid, false otherwise

canTransferFrom(address,address,address,.details: Does not check balances or access rights (Access Control).

params.value: The number of tokens to transfer.

returns._0: isCompliant True if the transfer complies with policy.

params.balanceToken_: Token contract that exposes `balanceOf` (must be a contract).
params.maxBalance_: Initial maximum balance per non-exempt address.

detectTransferRestriction(address,addres.details: See {ERC-1404} This function is where an issuer enforces the restriction logic of their token transfers.  Some examples of this might include: - checking if the token recipient is whitelisted,  - checking if a sender's tokens are frozen in a lock-up period, etc.

returns._0: uint8 restricted code, 0 means the transfer is authorized

detectTransferRestrictionFrom(address,ad.details: See {ERC-1404} Add an additionnal argument `spender` This function is where an issuer enforces the restriction logic of their token transfers.  Some examples of this might include: - checking if the token recipient is whitelisted,  - checking if a sender's tokens are frozen in a lock-up period, etc.

params.spender: The address initiating the delegated transfer.

returns._0: uint8 restricted code, 0 means the transfer is authorized
True when the address may hold any amount.

messageForTransferRestriction(uint8).details: See {ERC-1404} This function is effectively an accessor for the "message", a human-readable explanation as to why a transaction is restricted.

params.restrictionCode: The restriction code to translate into a message.

owner().details: Returns the address of the current owner.

pendingOwner().details: Returns the address of the pending owner.

remainingCapacity(address).details: Mirrors what {_detectTransferRestriction} computes, so an integrator can size a transfer without simulating it. Never reverts. This is the ERC-1404-flavoured wrapper over {BalanceCapManager._remainingCapacity}: the manager answers in booleans, the rule maps that to a restriction code.

returns.headroom: Remaining capacity in token units. `type(uint256).max` for an exempt address or the burn sentinel; meaningless when `restrictionCode` is non-zero.
returns.restrictionCode: `0` when the headroom is meaningful, otherwise the code a transfer would return.

removeExemptAddress(address).details: Reverts if the address is not exempt. The address keeps whatever it already holds; it simply cannot receive more once over the cap.

params.targetAddress: The address to bring back under the cap.

removeExemptAddresses(address[]).details: Addresses that are not exempt are skipped and counted rather than reverting.

params.targetAddresses: The addresses to bring back under the cap.

renounceOwnership().details: Leaves the contract without owner. It will not be possible to call `onlyOwner` functions. Can only be called by the current owner. NOTE: Renouncing ownership will leave the contract without an owner, thereby disabling any functionality that is only available to the owner.

params.newBalanceToken: The new token contract; must be a contract exposing `balanceOf`.

setMaxBalance(uint256).details: Lowering the cap does **not** claw back balances that already exceed it. Existing holders keep their tokens and may still send them away; they simply cannot receive more until they are back under the cap.
